description: [allAfrica] World Cotton Day should measure more than output. It should ask how much manufacturing, employment and African-owned value the continent creates from every bale it grows.
title: Africa: World Cotton Day - The Real Value of Africa's Cotton Comes After the Harvest

description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has urged parliamentarians to use their legislative and budgetary powers to strengthen health systems, reduce dependence on foreign aid and prepare for future pandemics.
title: Africa: WHO Chief Urges Parliamentarians to Cut Aid Dependency, Strengthen Pandemic Preparedness

description: [IFJ] According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), decent work means dignity, equality, fair remuneration and safe working conditions. However, all too often these conditions are not met in the media sector. Journalists and media workers often sacrifice their right to decent working conditions in the name of their vocation as a journalist, i.e. to serve democracy and uphold the public's right to information.
title: Africa: World Day for Decent Work - 'Journalists Should Recognise Themselves As Workers and Fight for Our Collective Struggles,' Says IFJ

description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United States has backed a stronger African Union-United Nations partnership to address conflicts across the continent, saying a UN framework for financing AU-led peace operations could provide a useful tool in responding to Africa's security crises.
title: Africa: U.S. Backs Stronger AU-UN Role in Africa Conflicts, Supports UN Financing for AU-Led Missions

description: [SNA] Khartoum -- Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Ambassador Mohi-Eddin Salem announced arrangements for an expected visit by the Chairperson of the African Union Commission (AUC) to Sudan to discuss Sudan's membership in the African Union, affirming that joint meetings will be held in this regard.
title: Africa: Foreign Minister - AU Commission Chairperson Expected to Visit Sudan to Discuss Membership

description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Ten clean energy projects across eight African countries are set to receive more than £2 million to expand renewable energy solutions in healthcare, telecommunications, agriculture, fishing and small businesses.
title: Africa: UK-Backed Clean Energy Projects to Scale Across Africa

description: [Liberian Observer] Chairman of Heirs Holdings, Tony Elumelu, has called for a fundamental shift in Africa's development model, urging the continent to move away from dependence on foreign aid toward trade, investment, entrepreneurship and private sector-led growth.
title: Africa: Elumelu Urges Africa to Shift From Aid Dependence to Trade and Investment

description: [Bird Story Agency] As World Cotton Day approaches on 7 October, Africa has an opportunity to consider how its cotton industry can contribute more to agricultural development, employment and economic growth. The opportunity extends far beyond producing and exporting raw cotton.
title: Africa: How Africa Can Capture More Value From Its Cotton

description: [Africa CDC] Addis Ababa -- The 54 WHO recognized African countries represent nearly 30% of WHO Membership. title: Africa: African Ministers to Convene Dialogue With WHO Director-General Candidates in Addis Ababa On 23 November 2026

title: East Africa: From Tigray to the Wider Horn of Africa - Ethiopia's Converging Conflicts, Rising Regional Risks

description: [The Conversation Africa] One of the hardest challenges in wildlife conservation arises when the habitat of a species in need of protection overlaps with land used by humans. Wolves and bears can kill livestock, elephants can damage homes and properties and wild boar can damage crops.
title: Africa: Protecting Endangered Species Must Include Supporting Habitats and Nearby Human Settlements

description: [The Conversation Africa] The 2026 Nobel prize for physics has been awarded to Francis Halzen for his discovery of high energy neutrino particles from space.

description: [The Conversation Africa] World leaders have been asked to support a proposed International Panel on Inequality. Brazil, Norway, South Africa and Spain, together with Nobel laureate Joseph Stiglitz, made the call on the margins of the UN General Assembly meeting in New York in September 2026.
title: Africa: The Global Panel On Inequality Needs African Evidence - Here's How It Could Work
